definition: A non-zero complex number written $z = r(\cos\theta + \mathrm{i}\sin\theta) = r\,\mathrm{cis}\,\theta$, where $r = \lvert z\rvert > 0$ is its modulus and $\theta = \arg z$ is its argument; also called modulus-argument form.

A non-zero complex number written $z = r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$, also called Euler form, with the same modulus $r = \lvert z\rvert > 0$ and argument $\theta$ as in polar form, and $\theta$ in radians.

The horizontal translation of a sinusoidal graph: in $f(x) = a\sin(b(x - c)) + d$ or $a\cos(b(x - c)) + d$ it is $c$, to the right when $c > 0$, so $a\cos(bx + B)$ with $b > 0$ is shifted $\frac{B}{b}$ to the left, not $B$.
